newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-LIONS FIRE COACH WAYNE FONTES.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-LIONS FIRE COACH WAYNE FONTES.

text.p: The Detroit Lions dismissed head coach Wayne Fontes on Thursday after eight full seasons and just one playoff win.
Lions owner William Clay Ford announced the firing in an afternoon news conference at the Silverdome after meeting with the coach Thursday morning.
The 57-year-old Fontes, who had one year left on his contract, has both the most wins (67) and the most losses (71) in team history.
"It's been a great eight years for Wayne Fontes," said Fontes, who spoke briefly at the end of the news conference but did not answer any questions.

"When I got here, people didn't care whether the Lions won or lost. Now people care. I'm going to keep on pumping the Detroit Lions. They've been like a family to me. Don't feel sorry for me. It's a chapter in my life that's over."
The only NFL coach who has been with his team longer than Fontes is Buffalo's Marv Levy. Fontes had been Detroit's head coach since December, 1988. Levy was named Bills coach in November, 1986.
The Lions started the 1996 season with four wins in their first six games, but lost nine of their next 10 to finish 5-11.
Much was expected of the Lions after they finished the 1995 season with a seven-game winning streak and a 10-6 record. Detroit was walloped by Philadelphia 58-37 in the wild card round.

"We got to the playoffs last year and had high hopes this year, but it didn't work out for us," said Ford. "I think we got good personnel. We have our shortcomings. With free agency, you lose key players from year to year. But I think we have a very talented team."

Fontes had taken the Lions to the playoffs in four of the last six years but had just one playoff victory. His best season was 1991, when he guided Detroit to a 12-4 record and a trip to the NFC championship game and was named the NFL's Coach of the Year.
Five NFL coaches have been fired and one stepped down over the last seven days.
